engines: Google AI Overviews and Perplexity, across the All Over Ointment and a sample of the catalog
lead: As of June 11, 2026, AI is largely accurate about Tubby Todd. We re-checked the questions parents ask across Google AI Overviews and Perplexity, and the engines state your hard facts correctly, including the active ingredient, the steroid-free and gluten-free status, newborn safety, the National Eczema Association seal, and both the fragrance-free and Lavender Rosemary versions. An earlier draft of this check flagged two problems on Perplexity, the fragrance answer and the treatment framing, and both had corrected themselves by the time we re-verified. That is exactly why a one-time check is only a snapshot and why monitoring is the real protection. The one item left is not an accuracy error. Google does not list Tubby Todd among its best for newborns picks.

score.note: AI gets your facts right across the products we checked. The only open item is a visibility omission on one Google list, not a wrong fact, so there is little to fix and a lot to protect.

areas.note: Hard specs and active ingredients are correct across the products we checked
AI cites your own site and the National Eczema Association
AI now describes the ointment as an eczema treatment and a moisturizer, which is right
AI names both the fragrance-free and the scented version when asked about fragrance

findings.query: is the All Over Ointment fragrance-free? (Perplexity, re-verified June 11)
findings.wrong: that it comes in a fragrance-free version and a separate Lavender Rosemary scented version, and that the scented one contains fragrance and lavender oils
findings.impact: This is correct today. An earlier draft caught Perplexity omitting the scented version, and it has since corrected, which is the kind of drift monitoring keeps honest.

findings.query: is it an eczema treatment or just a moisturizer? (Perplexity, re-verified June 11)
findings.wrong: that it is marketed as an eczema treatment and a moisturizer, not just a plain moisturizer
findings.truth: That matches how you position the product, an over-the-counter eczema treatment with 1% colloidal oatmeal.

findings.query: hard specs across the catalog (Google AI Overviews)
findings.wrong: the All Over Ointment at 1% colloidal oatmeal, Bye-Bye Cradle Cap at 0.95% pyrithione zinc, Sweet Cheeks Diaper Paste at 14% zinc oxide, and the Everyday Lotion scents
findings.truth: Every one of these matches your product pages, including the two over-the-counter drug actives.
findings.impact: This is what AI gets right, and the job is to keep it that way as your catalog changes.

findings.query: best baby eczema cream for newborns (Google AI Overviews, re-verified June 11)
findings.wrong: Google names Aveeno, Mustela, and CeraVe and leaves Tubby Todd off its best for newborns list.
findings.impact: This is a visibility gap, not a wrong fact about your product, and it is the hardest of these to move because it depends on the third-party sources Google ranks. We treat this as best-effort, not a guaranteed fix.
